items.title: GitHub moves `ubuntu-latest` to Ubuntu 26.04 in a phased rollout from 2026-10-19 to 2026-11-19 — all 60 CardiTrack jobs ride that label, none pins a version
items.text:
*HIGH* — GitHub moves `ubuntu-latest` to Ubuntu 26.04 in a phased rollout from 2026-10-19 to 2026-11-19 — all 60 CardiTrack jobs ride that label, none pins a version
Announced 2026-09-17 in runner-images #14748 (read directly). From 19 October the label may resolve to either Ubuntu 24.04 or 26.04 for a month, so a job can pass on one run and fail on the next. Every CardiTrack workflow uses `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` (60 occurrences across the deploy, infra, MedGemma, mobile, vendoring and digest workflows) and none pins `ubuntu-24.04` or `ubuntu-26.04`. GitHub's tool table shows no removals (OS 24.04.5 to 26.04.1, kernel 6.17 to 7.0), but the Android build installs a MAUI workload against the image's JDK and SDK, the tests run Testcontainers against the image's Docker, and the deploys use the image's gcloud, so a mid-rollout break would be intermittent and hard to attribute. Companion notices: Ubuntu 26.04 images are GA now (#14747) and the 22.04 images retire 2027-04-17 (#14254; not used here).
Smallest next action: pin `runs-on: ubuntu-24.04` across the workflows before 2026-10-19, or run one dev pipeline on `ubuntu-26.04` now and adopt it deliberately.

items.title: Firebase Apple SDK stops publishing to CocoaPods after October 2026; Firebase 13 will be Swift Package Manager and zip only — the binding chain under CardiTrack's iOS push
items.text:
*FYI* — Firebase Apple SDK stops publishing to CocoaPods after October 2026; Firebase 13 will be Swift Package Manager and zip only — the binding chain under CardiTrack's iOS push
The README on main and the FirebaseCore changelog (read directly) name 12.19.0 as the final scheduled CocoaPods release and describe 13.0.0 (unreleased, on main) as SPM/zip-only, needing Swift tools 6.2.1 and Xcode 26.2 or later, with iOS 15 minimum and the CocoaPods umbrella headers removed. Google's migration page (proxy-blocked; indexed) adds that CocoaPods itself goes read-only in December 2026. CardiTrack's own CI has no CocoaPods, so nothing breaks on the day. The exposure is the binding chain: `Plugin.Firebase.CloudMessaging` 4.0.1 depends on `AdamE.Firebase.iOS.CloudMessaging` ≥12.5.0.4 (NuGet registration, read directly), whose latest release is 12.10.0 from 2026-04-21. That binding wraps the native xcframeworks and must move to the SPM/zip artefacts for any 13.x, or iOS push stays on Firebase 12 while Apple's iOS 27 SDK rule (April 2027, recorded 2026-09-22) arrives.
Smallest next action: check whether the AdamE binding has a stated Firebase 13 plan; if not, decide to stay on the 12.x line through the Xcode 27 move and record that decision.
https://github.com/firebase/firebase-ios-sdk/blob/main/FirebaseCore/CHANGELOG.md

items.title: Auth0 10 KB user-profile limit: deprecated 2026-08-04, end of life 2027-03-04 — primary page found after three days held
items.text:
*FYI* — Auth0 10 KB user-profile limit: deprecated 2026-08-04, end of life 2027-03-04 — primary page found after three days held
Auth0's "Migrate Oversized User Profiles" page (indexed only; auth0.com is proxy-blocked) caps the serialised user profile, including user_metadata and app_metadata, at 10 KB. Until the EOL an extended allowance applies: writes over 10 KB but under it succeed and emit tenant-log warnings, and a tenant can adopt the new behaviour early under Tenant Settings > Advanced > Migrations ("Uncapped User Profile Data"). Warnings fire only on activity that updates the profile, so dormant oversized users are not surfaced. No CardiTrack code or Terraform writes user_metadata or app_metadata (grep), and the tenant's single post-login Action does verification gating, claims and social account linking, so profiles here are identity basics. Recorded because it is a dated end of life on the identity provider.
Smallest next action: search the Auth0 tenant logs for the oversized-profile warning event since 2026-08-04; none means close with no action.
https://auth0.com/docs/troubleshoot/product-lifecycle/deprecations-and-migrations/migrate-oversized-user-profiles

items.title: Google.Cloud.Storage.V1 5.0.0 (2026-09-21) moves resumable-upload checksum validation server-side and replaces the UploadValidationMode API — CardiTrack pins 4.15.0
items.text:
*FYI* — Google.Cloud.Storage.V1 5.0.0 (2026-09-21) moves resumable-upload checksum validation server-side and replaces the UploadValidationMode API — CardiTrack pins 4.15.0
Read directly from history.md and PR #15769. CRC32C validation moves from client-side-after-upload to server-side via an x-goog-hash header on the final chunk; UploadValidationMode.ThrowOnly and DeleteAndThrow are replaced by RejectAndThrow (old members obsoleted with guidance), and the public UploadValidationException is removed in favour of ordinary HTTP errors. CardiTrack's two callers, report storage and profile-photo storage, call UploadObjectAsync with default options and reference none of the changed members (grep across src and tests is empty), so the compile break is not on our path, and the behaviour change — a corrupted upload is rejected rather than deleted afterwards — is strictly better. 4.16.0 (2026-09-17) added an idempotency header only. No CVE, no deprecation date.
Smallest next action: take 5.0.0 on the next dependency bump and confirm the report and photo upload tests pass.
https://github.com/googleapis/google-cloud-dotnet/blob/main/apis/Google.Cloud.Storage.V1/docs/history.md

From the Firely release notes (read directly): PROFILE_ELEMENTDEF_SLICENAME_NOMATCH moves 10012→10018 and PROFILE_STRUCTURE_TYPE_MISSING 10014→10019, and the JSON and XML serialisers no longer write empty objects (`{}`) or empty elements (`<x/>`). CardiTrack's only production use is the FHIR R4 report renderer, which builds a Bundle and serialises it with System.Text.Json's ForFhir options; it does not switch on issue codes or run the validator, so only the empty-element change can alter emitted report JSON, and only if a bundle currently contains one. Before this run's window but never recorded. No CVE.

items.title: Ollama 0.40.0-rc0 introduces manifest-list storage and a lazy "compatibility migration" that rewrites legacy Gemma 3 GGUFs on first load — MedGemma 1.5 4B is on that list
items.text:
*FYI* — Ollama 0.40.0-rc0 introduces manifest-list storage and a lazy "compatibility migration" that rewrites legacy Gemma 3 GGUFs on first load — MedGemma 1.5 4B is on that list
Pre-release of 2026-09-25, read directly (release page, commit 75b9527, and the compatmigrate/ tree with gemma3.go, gemma3n.go, gemma4.go, embeddinggemma.go). The headline — MLX by default on Apple Silicon — is irrelevant to Cloud Run. The relevant change: runner-specific manifests coexist under one tag (manifest lists), and "legacy Ollama GGUFs" of the patched model families are migrated lazily into llama.cpp-compatible children on first use, preserving templates, projectors and split GGUFs. Our image bakes /root/.ollama at build time from the vendored medgemma-1.5-4b-it-Q4_K_M.gguf plus mmproj, asserts the name with `ollama list` and aliases with `ollama cp` — all three touch what changes, and a lazy rewrite inside a Cloud Run instance means cold-start work and container-filesystem writes the build never exercised. Nothing shifts today: the pin is 0.34.2 by digest, 0.34.4 is the latest stable with no security fixes, and the SSRF advisory GHSA-57p7-34ff-7w3w is unchanged.
Smallest next action: before any bump past 0.34.x, build the MedGemma image once against 0.40.0-rc0 and check the name assertion, first-request latency and /root/.ollama size.
https://github.com/ollama/ollama/releases/tag/v0.40.0-rc0

items.title: EU AI Act Article 50: the Commission's final transparency guidelines (2026-07-20) and the Code of Practice on AI-generated content (adequacy 2026-07-08) — the official answer sheet for open item OI-15 (c)
items.text:
*FYI* — EU AI Act Article 50: the Commission's final transparency guidelines (2026-07-20) and the Code of Practice on AI-generated content (adequacy 2026-07-08) — the official answer sheet for open item OI-15 (c)
Indexed only (digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu is proxy-blocked). The Art. 50 obligations have applied since 2026-08-02 and ai_act_classification.md §7.1 already treats them as live, with two open gaps: in-product disclosure across eight AI surfaces (issue #1244) and machine-readable marking of generated text (OI-15 (c)). Neither the guidelines — who must comply with interaction disclosure and content marking, and how to show it — nor the Code, which the Commission and the AI Board found adequate as the only EU-wide practical compliance tool for Art. 50(2), (4) and (5), is cited there. The Code is described as requiring multilayered machine-readable marking of AI-generated outputs. The DPIA records no EEA users today, so the exposure is prospective, not current.
Smallest next action: someone with browser access reads the guidelines' scope section and the Code's text-marking commitments, closes OI-15 (c) one way or the other, cites both in §7.1, and checks #1244's marking against the Code's wording rather than inventing one.

items.title: Draft Medical Devices (Amendment) Regulations 2026: the UK pre-market regime, expected to be laid Q4 2026 and to apply to GB market access around mid-2027 — includes a rule that claims must match the stated intended purpose
items.text:
*FYI* — Draft Medical Devices (Amendment) Regulations 2026: the UK pre-market regime, expected to be laid Q4 2026 and to apply to GB market access around mid-2027 — includes a rule that claims must match the stated intended purpose
Published for WTO comment on 2026-05-08 alongside an MHRA stakeholder impact survey (closed 2026-06-19); indexed only, gov.uk is proxy-blocked, and not on the record or in any compliance doc. Content as reported: essential requirements aligned to international practice, IMDRF-aligned IVD classification, technical-documentation retention, custom-made device traceability, and "requiring manufacturers to align claims about their medical devices with their statement of intended purpose". Expected laying in Parliament December 2026, in force for GB market access around June 2027, international reliance provisions 2028. No obligation for a product that is not a device, but two things to log: the timetable is the UKCA-side deadline OI-2 should plan against if the answer is "device", and the claims rule is the statutory form of the MHRA Ambient Voice precedent (recorded 2026-09-04) — website copy and the MedGemma tone block are the claims, the DPIA §3 intended-purpose wording is the anchor they must not exceed. Whether the draft touches software qualification or the Rule 11 equivalent is unverified.
Smallest next action: read the draft SI's software provisions; if it changes the qualification test or the Rule 11 equivalent, this becomes HIGH when laid.
https://www.gov.uk/government/news/mhra-invites-views-on-proposed-changes-to-medical-device-regulation
